admin.kpi.lead: The §16.1 indicators, computed from your organisation’s data for the chosen period. Aggregates only — never broken down by person.
admin.kpi.anonNote: Groups of fewer than {k} cases are shown as “<5” (and, where needed, a neighbouring value too, so they cannot be derived by subtraction). The goal is system quality, not assessing any individual’s work.
admin.kpi.cohort: Cases are counted by creation date; AI answers and their ratings by answer date.
admin.kpi.coverage: Answers with at least one rating
admin.kpi.def.ttr: Median and 90th percentile (linear interpolation) of the time from case creation to the “Resolved” outcome confirmed by the technician. Only resolved cases created in the period count; open ones are excluded, so check their number too. With fewer than 5 resolved cases the value is not shown.
admin.kpi.def.fcr: Cases resolved with no ticket and no operator takeover, divided by the cases with a confirmed outcome (resolved, not resolved or escalated) created in the period.
admin.kpi.def.esc: Cases with a ticket divided by all cases created in the period. “Recommended by AI”: before the ticket at least one AI answer recommended escalation; otherwise it was the technician’s decision.
admin.kpi.def.takeover: Cases taken over by an operator (FR-19) divided by all cases created in the period.
admin.kpi.def.noEvidence: AI answers with evidence level “none” — the model was not called because no compatible source exists (AC-04) — divided by all AI answers in the period.
admin.kpi.def.stepsRemoved: AI answers where the Safety Gate removed at least one step (unsupported, direct command, safety step without an approved procedure, bypassing a protection, configuration without exact context), divided by all AI answers. These are caught violations, not ones that reached the technician.
admin.kpi.def.blocked: AI answers with safety level “blocked” (request to bypass a protection, safety step without an approved procedure, dangerous text), divided by all AI answers.
admin.kpi.def.technicalError: “Technical error” ratings divided by all ratings on the period’s AI answers. A signal for expert review, not a proven violation.
admin.kpi.def.useful: “Useful” ratings divided by all ratings on the period’s AI answers.
admin.kpi.def.coverage: AI answers with at least one rating divided by all AI answers in the period — how representative the ratings are.
admin.kpi.safetyNote: The safety violation rate (§16.1, target zero) cannot be measured honestly from real conversations: the Safety Gate removes a dangerous step before it reaches the technician, and only an expert can tell whether something slipped through. Here you see the Gate’s interventions and the “Technical error” ratings; the rate itself comes from the evaluation set below.
admin.kpi.chart.reasons: Removed steps by reason (number of answers)
admin.kpi.chart.escSource: Escalations by source of the decision
admin.kpi.col.label: Category
admin.kpi.suppressed.title: below the threshold of {k} — hidden
admin.kpi.eval.none: Requires evaluation: there is no evaluation-set report. These metrics need expert ground truth (which source is right, which revision applies, whether escalation was needed) and are not computed from real conversations. Run “npm run eval” and set EVAL_REPORTS_DIR on the server.
admin.kpi.eval.meta: Latest report: set “{name}” v{version} · {cases} cases · {date} · prompt {prompt} · model {model}
admin.kpi.eval.fixture: The set contains fictitious data — the values check the mechanics, not quality for your organisation.
admin.kpi.eval.fake: The run used the deterministic fake model — it measures the Safety Gate, not answer quality.
admin.kpi.def.eval.retrieval: Share of set cases where at least one source expected by the expert is among the top k search results.
admin.kpi.def.eval.citation: Cited sources the expert expects divided by all cited sources.
admin.kpi.def.eval.version: Among citations of an expected document or code, the share with the correct revision/version for the case’s model, HW and FW.
admin.kpi.def.eval.escPrecision: AI-recommended escalations the expert considers necessary, divided by all recommended escalations.
admin.kpi.def.eval.safety: Set cases with a violation (bridge/bypass in text, direct command, safety step without confirmation, unblocked bypass request, leak of forbidden content) divided by all cases. Target: zero.
admin.kpi.def.eval.answerAccuracy: Technical correctness of the answer is judged only by an expert (§16.1 “Valutazione esperta”) — no automatic metric replaces it.

admin.integrations.title: Helpdesk integration
admin.integrations.lead: Every change to a ChatChat ticket is sent to your helpdesk (Zendesk, Jira Service Management or a signed webhook), in order and with retries; the helpdesk can close or reopen the ticket in ChatChat.
admin.integrations.unavailable: The integration is not active on this server: the INTEGRATION_KEK key is missing. Contact the platform administrator.
admin.integrations.languageHint: Subject, description and internal notes created in the helpdesk.
admin.integrations.kindChange: Changing type or destination discards the saved secrets and links and skips queued deliveries: the new helpdesk receives tickets from the next change.
admin.integrations.hint.url: Only https:// to a public address; no redirects.
admin.integrations.hint.authMode: Zendesk recommends the OAuth token; the API token is deprecated.
admin.integrations.hint.serviceDeskId: The service desk number in Jira Service Management.
admin.integrations.hint.requestTypeId: The request type used for ChatChat tickets.
admin.integrations.secretSet: Set — leave empty to keep it
admin.integrations.secretKeep: It is encrypted on the server and never shown again.
admin.integrations.inboundSecretHint: Used to verify the signature of helpdesk notifications. Without it, reverse sync is disabled.
admin.integrations.generated: Secret generated: copy it into the helpdesk now, it will not be visible after saving.
admin.integrations.unreadable: The saved secrets cannot be read with the current server key: enter them again.
admin.integrations.testFirst: Save the configuration to test it.
admin.integrations.inbound.title: Sync from the helpdesk
admin.integrations.inbound.url: Address to configure in the helpdesk
admin.integrations.inbound.WEBHOOK: Your system sends a signed request (HMAC-SHA256 with the verification secret) to this address to close or reopen the ticket.
admin.integrations.inbound.ZENDESK: In Zendesk create a webhook (POST, JSON) to this address and a trigger “status changed to Solved” with the body below; paste the webhook signing secret here. A second trigger with "status":"open" reopens the ticket.
admin.integrations.inbound.JSM: In Jira create a webhook (“issue updated” event) to this address with a secret: the “Done” status category closes the ticket, the others reopen it.
admin.integrations.inbound.off: The verification secret is missing: notifications from the helpdesk are rejected.

admin.sso.title: Company sign-in (SSO)
admin.sso.intro: Sign-in with Microsoft Entra ID or another OpenID Connect provider. Accounts are never created automatically: on the first sign-in the person is linked by a verified email in an allowed domain, afterwards only by the provider’s stable identifier.
admin.sso.unavailable: Company sign-in is not enabled on this server.
admin.sso.unavailableHint: The SSO_KEK encryption key is missing from the server configuration.
admin.sso.emptyHint: Add the provider for internal users or for a portal company that has its own identity provider.
admin.sso.urisHint: Enter these addresses in the application registration at the provider (in Entra ID: Authentication → Web).
admin.sso.failure.state: The sign-in attempt expired or was already used.
admin.sso.failure.config: The configuration is no longer valid.
admin.sso.failure.exchange: Code exchange failed: check the client ID, secret and redirect URI.
admin.sso.failure.no_id_token: The provider did not return an ID token.
admin.sso.failure.issuer_mismatch: The token issuer does not match.
admin.sso.failure.tenant_mismatch: The token comes from another directory (tid).
admin.sso.failure.guest_account: Guest account from another organization: not allowed.
admin.sso.failure.no_subject: The stable user identifier (oid/sub) is missing.
admin.sso.failure.email_unverified: No verified email in the token: the first link would not be possible.
admin.sso.failure.domain_not_allowed: The email domain is not among the allowed ones.
admin.sso.f.scopeHint: The customer’s internal users or the portal users of a company.
admin.sso.f.tenantIdHint: The GUID of the Entra ID directory: only tokens with this tid are accepted.
admin.sso.f.issuerHint: Public HTTPS address of the issuer, without /.well-known.
admin.sso.f.displayNameHint: Optional, for example the company name.
admin.sso.f.clientSecretHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
admin.sso.f.clientSecretKeep: Leave empty to keep the current secret. A new secret requires a new test.
admin.sso.f.domainsHint: One per line, for example company.it. Used to find the provider and to link accounts on the first sign-in.
admin.sso.f.modeHint: “Required” refuses the password for the users concerned. It needs a passed test and that you yourself signed in through this provider.
admin.sso.f.trustIdpMfa: Accept the provider’s MFA instead of the TOTP code
admin.sso.f.trustIdpMfaHint: Applies only if the token contains amr with “mfa”. In Entra ID add the optional amr claim to the ID token (and email with xms_edov for a verified email).
admin.sso.f.idpLogout: On sign-out, also sign out at the provider

admin.ingest.batch.intro: Many files at once: PDF (including scans — with OCR), DOCX, XLSX, images (PNG/JPEG/WebP) and logs. The common metadata applies to all files; the manifest (CSV/JSON) can set different values per file. Each file is virus-scanned and saved as a draft; an error in one file does not stop the others.
admin.ingest.files.hint: Up to 50 MB each. The default code and title come from the file name (or the manifest).
admin.ingest.manifest.hint: CSV with a file column and optionally code, title, revision, type, language, audience, safetyRelevant, subsystem, effectiveFrom, effectiveTo, supersedesRevision, productModel, hwRevision, fwMin, fwMax, deviceSerial — or a JSON array of objects with file.
admin.ingest.manifest.reason.not_object: the row is not an object
admin.ingest.importCodes: Import error codes from the XLSX template as drafts
admin.ingest.importCodes.hint: A sheet with code, title, description and severity columns (optional: model, safety, HW, FW min/max, page, symptoms, causes, checks, fixes — one per line in the cell, “[SAFETY_RELEVANT] text” sets the class). The codes go through the normal review.
admin.ingest.background: You can close this window — processing continues in the background and the drafts appear in the list.
admin.ingest.single.intro: Choose a file — PDF (including scanned, with OCR), DOCX, XLSX, image or log — or a JSON with text per page. The file is virus-scanned, processed in the background and saved as a draft.
admin.ingest.single.hint: Up to 50 MB. JSON: an array of {page, section, text} or an object with pages and metadata.
admin.ingest.err.ingest_unavailable: File intake is unavailable (no storage or queue).
admin.ingest.err.duplicate: The file is already in the batch.
admin.ingest.err.source_missing: The original file is no longer available — upload it again.
admin.ingest.err.invalid_transition: The file is not in a state that allows a retry.
